items.title: 63476_Jimmie Crawford oral history interview
items.q: Breathing. Yeah, Trummy used to stand around, blowing in that bottle. I used to look at him

ctx.x: Breathing. Yeah, Trummy used to stand around, blowing in that bottle. I used to look at him, I wasn't too down with anybody that always applied themselves too religiously about practicing. Me, I wasn't practicing, that's why I was a dumb -- I was a good player, but I didn't -- practice? No. That's why I'm going to get on my single strokes, get my fingers fast.

I don't play now, but in case I do get a call for a job or a show, I'll take it. See, Ernie Royal, the trumpet player, Frank West, the tenor saxophone player, they told me sometime ago that they never would take a Broadway musical again. Says, they don't play music. Who did I look up and see grabbing shows and anything they could get? Ernie Royal and Frank West. And I told them about it. I say, I thought you were not going to play any more Broadway musicals.

items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: And the drummer, Jimmy Crawford, somebody told me that he taught Crawford in school in Memphis

ctx.x: -- you know, but he was -- he was more of a school teacher type person, and that's what he did before -- before he organized, got that band.

I understand -- I wasn't with him then, but I understand that some of the guys came right out of school with him, out of Fisk, you know. And the drummer, Jimmy Crawford, somebody told me that he taught Crawford in school in Memphis, and when Jimmy left school, he went to teaching, you know. But Jimmy Wilcox, Willie Smith, Earl Caruthers and some other guys was in the band before that I didn't meet -- Andrew Brown. They all went to Fisk University together.
Why, had they had the band in college or were they just friends in college?
